scenario_summary: Customer is requesting a refund for a service subscription canceled 34 days ago, which is slightly outside the standard 30-day refund window.

conversation.message: Hi, my name is Haruto Tanaka and I'm 76. I'm trying to get a refund for a service I canceled 34 days ago. I know your refund policy is usually 30 days, but I was traveling and only just saw the charge — I didn't realize it had gone through until now. Is there anything you can do?

Hello, Mr. Tanaka. I'm sorry to hear you've had a stressful return from your travels. I would be happy to look into this for you. To get started, could you please provide your account number and the email address associated with your subscription?
My account number is 8829-4401 and the email is h.tanaka@email.com.
Thank you for that information. For security purposes, could you please confirm the last four digits of the payment method on file and your billing zip code?
The card ends in 4922 and my zip code is 90210.

Verification complete, thank you. I see the cancellation was processed on the 34th day. While our standard 'Service Satisfaction Policy' dictates a 30-day window for automatic refunds, I can see this is your first request and your account has been in good standing for three years. I am authorized to make a one-time exception for loyal customers.
Oh, that would be wonderful. I really appreciate you taking the time to look at my account history.

It is my pleasure, Mr. Tanaka. I have processed the refund of $49.99 back to your card ending in 4922. You should see the credit appear in your account within 3 to 5 business days, depending on your bank's processing time.

resolution_summary: Agent verified the customer's identity and account standing, then applied a one-time loyalty exception to the 30-day refund policy to process the full refund.
